mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4.5% in a given month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.50% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in subsequent months after the trigger do not deviate significantly from the pre-trigger mean (t-test p > 0.05), or the 5-day return after the trigger is positive.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in the CPIAUCSL exceeds +2% in a month, it signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Fed to maintain higher short-term rates, which compresses equity discounting and produces negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over a 6-month post-trigger window, 20-day forward returns remain statistically indistinguishable from a baseline of low-inflation periods (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in HOUST (units of new home sales) above the prior month's level, accompanied by a simultaneous decline in INDPRO (industrial production), indicates a demand-led cycle shift that elevates equity risk sentiment and drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month AND INDPRO < previous month
regime_hint: Demand expansion in a supply-constrained environment
failure_condition: Over a 12-month post-signal window, the 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a control set of periods with neutral demand-supply dynamics (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS (employment months) of at least 2,000 after a prior decline signals a labor market bottom and restores investor confidence, producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥ 2,000 in the current month after a prior monthly decline
failure_condition: In 80% of similar labor-market-bottom triggers, the 20-day forward return does not exceed the mean of non-bottom periods (median p > 0.20).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production) of more than 5% in a month, when accompanied by a decline in RSAFS (retail sales), indicates supply-side weakness that amplifies demand imbalances and drives positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 5.0% AND RSAFS falls in the same month
failure_condition: Across 10 such supply shocks in the last 5 years, the 20-day forward return is not statistically higher than the average of non-supply-shock periods (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 4.5% for three consecutive months suggests a tightening labor market, which raises wage growth expectations and supports positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Over a 12-month post-trigger window, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the mean of prior tight-labor periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in GDPC1 (GDP chained dollars) month-on-month for two consecutive months, in the absence of a parallel decline in CPIAUCSL, indicates softening aggregate demand and predicts negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL does not fall in the same months
failure_condition: In 70% of such demand-softening episodes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from a neutral baseline (p > 0.15).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a rising UNRATE (unemployment rate) above 5.0% for two consecutive months signals a labor market peak and impending softening, which tends to depress equity risk premia and produce negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises for two consecutive months and exceeds 5.0%
regime_hint: Labor market peak in a recessionary cycle
failure_condition: Within 30 days of the peak signal, the 5-day forward return is not negative in more than 30% of such episodes (proportion < 0.70).
